stem.en: Kabir cuts a stem of the moong plant and puts it in water, and it grows roots. He asks why "a cut-off finger does not grow a person". What is the difference?

text.en: The cutting has meristems and cells whose pages can be reopened toward root; a finger's cells are committed, with their unneeded pages locked tight, and it has only a few stem cells for skin and bone. A plant's cells keep more options open.

feedback.en: A plant's cells are not simpler. They keep their chromatin more reopenable, from VI.6, which is a difference in switches, not complexity.
A finger in water grows nothing. The cutting grows because its cells can become root.

text.en: A finger has no DNA for a whole person.

feedback.en: Every finger cell has the whole tape, from Gurdon. The pages are locked, not missing.

explanation.en: Regrowth depends on how firmly a cell's switches are set. Plant cells reset more easily than animal cells, and animals keep few reserves.
